account:
Today I attended my morning office business and came to the mill for the scheduled ten-o'clock grain inspection. The secretary reported no new business awaiting a decision. I have personally checked the mill stall chest: it contains 128 hay bales, equivalent to 1,152 wheat, with a posted price of two emeralds per bale. I have not established who is responsible for the inspection or verified delivery and storage conditions.

The unusual news is a repeated report of a 'bridge or port change' discussed at the bakery. Townsfolk 01 said baker and freight were there, and another version included neighbour. Several other townsfolk repeat the same phrase, but repetition does not establish independent firsthand evidence. The secretary explicitly regards the report as unverified and has no firsthand evidence of a defect or authorized new work. I do not yet know what change was proposed, whether anyone agreed to it, or whether anything has actually happened.

Residents also report seeing baker carrying sacks of bread at the inn and elsewhere, and wheat at the bakery. Those movements could simply be ordinary baking and deliveries; I have no evidence of wrongdoing. The bakery discussion might concern transport, access, or freight arrangements, but that is only a possibility, not an established purpose. Separately, I instructed builder to inspect the bridge and street lighting and report defects and costs, without authorizing paid work. I cannot yet connect that instruction to the bakery discussion. I intend to seek direct explanations from baker, freight, and neighbour while keeping my appointments, rather than treating rumour as fact.
